newsitem.title: UK: Russia has new anthrax toxin, nerve agents-Jane's.
newsitem.headline: Russia has new anthrax toxin, nerve agents-Jane's.

text.p: Russia has developed a new variant of the anthrax toxin that is totally resistant to antibiotics and which could cause a catastrophe if it fell into the wrong hands, Jane's said on Thursday.

The foreword to the influential Jane's Land Based Air Defence 1997-98 defence publication said the toxin, along with three new nerve agents, had been developed by Russian military research laboratories.

"It only needs this, or the new chemical nerve agents to be independently discovered by an ostracised nation's scientists and then developed for missile delivery for an Armageddon situation to occur whereby the only reliable retribution may well be overwhelming nuclear response," it said.
The publication said the three nerve agents could be made without using any of the precursor chemicals which are banned under the 1993 Chemical Weapons Convention.
It said reports of the anthrax toxin and the three new nerve agents had come from defectors and western intelligence sources.
Two of the new nerve agents were eight times as deadly as the VX nerve agent which Iraq has acknowledged stockpiling while the other was as deadly as VX, it said. Jane's gave no more details.

Anthrax is usually carried by sheep and cows. It can be contracted by human beings and those affected can develop festering boils and die in agony unless treated quickly. The West still has lingering concerns that Russia, Iraq and other states may still have stocks of banned biological weapons despite signing the 1972 Biological Weapons Convention.
Delegates from nearly 140 states which have signed the pact are trying to finally put teeth into the treaty, which bans a whole category of weapons of mass destruction.
